T880 (does a row's declared holds reach the store, and does the confirmation line say what actually landed?) — answered: NO for space-separated lists, and the confirmation line lied in both cases. Fixed in src/managent/main.zig; regression tools/regression-bundle-header-parse.sh wired into build.zig; live-store backfill applied via holds --sync; red-then-green evidence in findings/T880-context.json.

DEFECT (measured, pre-fix): parseBundleMeta tokenizes the bundle header on spaces, so `holds=a.zig b.zig c.zig` registered only a.zig — two files silently dropped, no warning — while the registration confirmation printed `holds a.zig` whether one hold or three landed (both add paths, line 3709/3827-era code). Live cost: T872 (green-up delete wave) declared four space-separated holds (src/vb_fixpoint.zig bin/argus tools/orcha-acceptance.sh build.zig), store row carried ZERO; T877 lost two of three (store [tools/runner] vs bundle-declared [tools/runner,src/managent/main.zig,tools/facts]). The one-writer guard protected nothing it claimed to.

FIX (one surface, one defect class per the brief):
1. parseBundleMeta — list-valued keys (holds=/needs=/caps=) accept space-separated values via bare-token continuation: a token without '=' following a list key extends that list. Two fences: once `acceptance=` appears (its value runs to end of line, T217), bare tokens belong to the acceptance command, never a list; any other `key=...` token ends the run.
2. readBundleHolds (the sync + vacuous-guard path, same truncation) — reads the whole rest of the line up to the next KNOWN key token / -->, splitting on commas AND whitespace. isKnownMetaKey stops at a real following key (set holds needs caps deliverables acceptance accepts duty due_after shape context exclude priority waiting), never at a path containing '='.
3. parseDeliverablesFromBundle (header path) — `deliverables=a.zig b.zig` used to fold into ONE element "a.zig b.zig" (a path that can never exist; done refused loudly with an unreadable message). Now space/comma-split with the same next-known-key stop. (Different defect shape from holds/needs: LOUD at done-time, not silent data loss — reported per the probe.)
4. Confirmation line — new holdsSetLabel prints EVERY hold that landed and the count: `set: A, holds 3 (a.zig, b.zig, c.zig)`; one hold: `holds 1 (a.zig)`; none: `set: A`, never an empty list as a false path.
5. suggest — template now carries `holds=` (was `deliverables=-->` only), so a suggest-minted bundle (the T872 shape: minted by suggest which dropped holds entirely — B24) has the placeholder the author fills before holds --sync.

PER-FIELD PROBE (probe and report, not assumed):
- holds=: SHARES the defect (space-truncation + lying confirmation). FIXED.
- needs=: SHARES the defect (same token loop — `needs=T1 T2` stored only T1). FIXED.
- deliverables=: SHARES a defect but a different shape — space-separated values fold into ONE element with embedded spaces ("a.zig b.zig"), which fails LOUDLY at done-time (git check refuses) rather than silently dropping files. FIXED in the header path of parseDeliverablesFromBundle.
- SIBLING PARSERS (report-only, out of the brief's one-surface scope): tools/git-commit-mine-lib.sh, tools/orcha-acceptance.sh:185, tools/dispatch_verify.py, tools/model-profiles.py each parse deliverables= with the same stop-at-first-whitespace truncation as the old managent parser. A space-separated deliverables= list is still truncated to its first element for commit-scope and dispatch-verify. Smallest honest follow-up: a shared parse (or at minimum the same known-key stop) across the four; a follow-up task should own it.

NO-SET-VERB FINDING (the brief asked): no verb can set holds on an existing row arbitrarily. The writers are: add (bundle/--holds), suggest (empty), holds --sync (bundle-sourced only). A row whose bundle declares no holds= can never acquire holds after registration. The absence is real; the smallest honest fix is a `holds <id> --set a,b,c` verb (mirroring `needs <id> --add`), which would also have let T872/T877 be backfilled without a bundle edit. holds --sync (existing) was the backfill path used here.
